content.summary: Palliative and end-of-life care guidance for patients with advanced heart failure, focusing on symptom relief, psychological support, advanced care planning, and regular symptom assessment.
key_points: Frequent assessment of symptoms (including dyspnoea and pain) resulting from advanced heart failure and comorbidities; focus on symptom relief.
Provide access to psychological support and spiritual care for patient and family as needed.
Advanced care planning: document preferences for place of death and resuscitation; may include deactivation of devices such as ICDs or long-term MCS after multidisciplinary decision.
Focus on improving or maintaining quality of life (QOL) of patient and family until death.

symptom_assessment.recommendation: Perform symptom assessment on a regular basis in addition to clinical assessment.

breathlessness.recommendation: Repeat doses of opioids may be considered for relief of dyspnoea, although effectiveness is not demonstrated.
considerations: Guide patients about opioid side effects: constipation, nausea, urinary retention, mental status changes.
Benzodiazepines may be considered as second- or third-line treatment when opioids and non-pharmacological measures fail.
Increasing inspired oxygen concentration may provide relief.

pain.recommendation: Non-pharmacologic management can be helpful; opioids are generally viewed as safe options.

anxiety_and_depression.recommendation: Adequate conventional treatment should be offered.

advance_care_planning_and_documentation.recommendation: Proactive decisions and advanced planning regarding palliative and end-of-life care should be documented, regularly reviewed, and communicated to all involved in the patient's care.
advance_care_planning_and_documentation.notes: Healthcare providers should ensure patient and carer preferences are followed when possible; recognize some patients may be unable to express preferences due to depression or cognitive impairment.
